trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6); going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.

Going to number 2 would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes left.
The line must go up: down is number 5, which comes later.
Cell (2,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,2). So the line goes up.
The line must go left: up is number 6, which comes later.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 5; going down, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,4). So the line goes up.
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down would strand number 5: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
